item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00141","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C06","C20","C02"],"selected_candidate_label":"C06","confidence":0.93,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C06 is a highly plausible drafting source because it concerns the same 1959 steel negotiations, expresses the same governing position, and uses closely parallel language: settlement should remain with the parties through voluntary collective bargaining; federal intervention is reserved for emergencies affecting national health or safety; and the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service is available to help the parties reach agreement. The child expands this compact framework after the strike has begun, adding updated consequences and a stronger demand for intensive bargaining. C20 and C02 provide additional close models for presidential appeals to labor and management, but neither matches the child's legal-policy framework and immediate factual setting as closely as C06.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Disputes between labor and management must be settled by collective bargaining between the parties. It is only when the national safety and health are imperiled that Federal law should be invoked.","parent_excerpt":"Congress in the Taft-Hartley Act authorized the President, in emergencies affecting the national health or safety, to appoint boards of inquiry... I think that you and I are in agreement that free voluntary collective bargaining is an integral part of the American democratic way of life.","explanation":"Both state the same two-part policy: voluntary collective bargaining is primary, while federal emergency machinery is reserved for threats to national health or safety."},{"child_excerpt":"All these weeks the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service has been attempting to assist the parties to reach agreement.","parent_excerpt":"Congress has also provided for conciliation and mediation through the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service, and that Service stands ready at any time to assist the parties to reach agreement.","explanation":"The child closely reuses the parent’s description of the Service's role and the phrase 'assist the parties to reach agreement,' updated to reflect its subsequent activity."},{"child_excerpt":"The Steelworkers and the steel companies must find that way expeditiously.","parent_excerpt":"I suggest to both parties to this dispute that they continue to bargain... until all of the terms and conditions of a new contract are agreed upon.","explanation":"Both letters culminate in a direct presidential appeal to the same steel labor and management parties to continue bargaining toward their own agreement."}]}
